rulings.rationale: Ministry data confirms that Midgard's maize imports from Orvan remained resilient in October due to delayed delivery terms (ORV-0030/P14) before experiencing a sharp decline by December, resulting in a quarterly YoY loss of USD 126.4M.

supporting_citations.quote: The October volume held up longer than the wheat routes because a share of the maize trade was on delayed delivery terms.

odin_ranges.metric_definition: Aggregate year-on-year change in import value from Orvan for Oct-Dec 2026 vs Oct-Dec 2025.
assumptions: The Orvan trade gap represents the primary exposure before accounting for partial offsets from more expensive substitutes.
odin_ranges.uncertainty_note: Both advocates utilize the same calculated gross loss of USD 156.5M for the Orvan route. While mitigation exists, no aggregate quarterly calculation for the net offset was provided.

odin_ranges.metric_definition: Aggregate year-on-year change in import value from Orvan for Oct-Dec 2026 vs Oct-Dec 2025.
assumptions: Initial resilience in October buffered the impact, but the full loss was felt by December.
odin_ranges.uncertainty_note: The quarterly loss is well-documented by Tier 1 data and verified by calculation.

odin_ranges.metric_definition: Aggregate year-on-year change in import value from Orvan for Oct-Dec 2026 vs Oct-Dec 2025.
assumptions: Vanir shipments provide a small offset but do not meaningfully shift the scale of the Orvan-related exposure.
odin_ranges.uncertainty_note: Tolan's data comes from Tier 2 sources (Harbour Review) but is consistent with the trends seen in Midgard's Tier 1 data.
